plans.title: Young Hall, floor 2
plans.how: Traced from a photo of the evacuation plan posted on this floor. The photo was squared up from the sign's frame; walls are its dark lines, corridors its white spaces, rooms its gray boxes; stairs are the hatched boxes, elevators the crossed boxes, restrooms the boxes with the restroom icon. Room numbers were read by OCR and checked by hand. The sign has no scale, so its building outline was fitted to the mapped outline (with north as its NORTH arrow shows).

fit.transform: similarity, sign outline fitted to the building outline (ICP), then stretched along the building grid to match its walls

notes: Hand fixes: three wall cuts where the photo shows the lecture-hall walls with gaps, and CS24 labeled by hand (the 2250B label sat at its edge).

plans.title: Young Hall floor 4

source.what: "Fourth Floor Plan" from the architects' UCLA Young Hall chemistry lab feasibility study: full floor with walls, corridors, stairs, elevators, restrooms and the bridge to the adjacent building; the project area is shaded; no room numbers, no scale bar
source.license: architect's portfolio image, copyright Paul Murdoch Architects; used here only to trace wall positions

plans.how: Architects' plan with no scale bar. The plan's long bar runs top to bottom, so it is turned 90 degrees (north is to the plan's left); with the rotation fixed, a scale sweep of the footprint against the building outline is best at 10.5 cm/px (median 1.05 m, 90% within 4.7 m). Orientation check: the floor 2 trace's elevator, stair and two restrooms land within 5 to 30 px (0.5 to 3 m) of the same cores on this plan. Four synthetic control points carry that transform.

notes: Architects' feasibility-study plan (2019): no room numbers and no scale bar, so rooms are traced without numbers; stairs, elevators and restrooms labeled by hand from the plan's own callouts. The 'PROJECT AREA 8,850 GSF' shading is the study's lab area, not a room.

Georeference: the plan is drawn with north to the left; it is turned 90 degrees and scaled by a sweep of the footprint against the building outline (best 10.5 cm/px, median 1.05 m).
